preferences.condition: The user has not explicitly specified a format.
preferences.instruction: When no output format is specified, prefer PNG for research figures suited to raster output; provide PDF/SVG for publication layouts or explicit vector requests.

preferences.condition: The figure contains data, parameter groups, or uncertainty estimates.
preferences.instruction: Label axes with physical quantities and units; identify parameter groups in the legend and explain the statistical meaning of error bars.
Use consistent colors for the same physical quantity across figures, choose colors accessible to readers with color-vision deficiencies, and add line styles to distinguish series.
Keep the original data and a standalone plotting script. Explain filtering, normalization, and fitting ranges, and do not hide inconsistent results for appearance.

preferences.condition: Writing a technical note for this Demo user.
preferences.instruction: First query the Persona knowledge relevant to the topic. Clearly explain concepts that are unrecorded or rated only as aware, and connect them to existing knowledge.

preferences.condition: Introducing equations, abbreviations, or new notation.
preferences.instruction: Define new symbols at first use, and explain the physical meaning, assumptions, and scope of equations in the surrounding prose.

preferences.condition: Organizing the body of a note.
preferences.instruction: Develop arguments in connected paragraphs. Use lists for logical groupings, avoiding a separate line for every sentence and unnecessary line breaks.

preferences.condition: Summarizing paper conclusions, numerical results, or conjectures.
preferences.instruction: Distinguish conclusions from sources, your own derivations, and questions awaiting verification. Retain traceable source references when citing materials.

preferences.condition: No other language or existing algorithm framework has been explicitly specified.
preferences.instruction: Prefer the Julia ITensor ecosystem for tensor-network algorithms: ITensors.jl for basic tensor operations, and ITensorMPS.jl for MPS/MPO objects and related algorithms.

preferences.condition: Adding an algorithm implementation or changing the model definition.
preferences.instruction: Validate small systems before large calculations. Where feasible, compare energies or representative observables with exact diagonalization, and check normalization and model conventions.

preferences.condition: Using approximate algorithms or interpreting physical results obtained from them.
preferences.instruction: Check convergence separately with respect to bond dimension, truncation threshold, time step, and system size. Report the checks actually performed and the remaining errors.
Save the Julia version, Project.toml, Manifest.toml, random seeds, parameter files, and code version so results can be reproduced.

preferences.condition: Preparing batch or long-running calculations; the script name is a Demo example and does not describe an actual server configuration.
preferences.instruction: Under the Demo's fictional protocol, prepare submission through scripts/submit_job.sh and a parameter file. First inspect the script and dry-run support, then state the resources and output paths. If the script is missing, say so; do not assume a real cluster provides this entry point.

preferences.condition: Saving results or continuing an existing job.
preferences.instruction: Save data, logs, and checkpoints under a unique run ID without overwriting other runs. Verify the model, parameters, and dependency versions before resuming a calculation.
